title: 10 Snipping Tool Hacks Every Windows 11 User Should Know
description: The humble Snipping Tool is great for beginners and power users alike.
fullText:
Snipping Tool is the default app for screenshots in Windows 11. There's a lot more to the app than that, however: With it, you can take screen recordings, extract text from images or websites that disable copying, and use a reverse image search tool. While ShareX is still my favorite app for taking screenshots in Windows, I think Snipping Tool has reached a point where it's great for both beginners and power users. Here are 10 essential Snipping Tool hacks that every Windows 11 user should know.

Copying text from images is one of the most common uses of screenshot tools, and Snipping Tool does it quite well. You can right-click any image in Windows 11, and go to Open with > Snipping Tool. Once the photo opens, you can click the Scan Text button to select all the text in the image. Windows will take a few moments to identify all the text in the photo, and, when it's ready, you can click Copy all text from the popover menu. You're also free to select a single sentence or block of text by clicking and dragging the cursor over it, and you can right-click this selection to reveal the Copy text button.

If all you want to do is copy text from sites that disable copying, interface elements in an app, or PDFs of scanned pages where you can't select the text easily, then you should use Snipping Tool to select and copy text without even taking a screenshot. This allows you to reduce unwanted image clutter by skipping the "taking a screenshot" step, and jumping straight to extracting text. To try this, open the Snipping Tool app in your Windows PC, and click the Text extractor button in the toolbar. You can click and drag over an area of the screen that contains text, and the app will automatically select it in a moment or two. Click Copy all text in the popover menu, and you're done.

Snipping Tool allows you to do some basic image editing, which you can use to automatically redact sensitive information from screenshots. Open any screenshot in Snipping Tool, and click Scan text. Once the tool scans for text, a popover menu will appear. You can select Quick redact here to automatically hide all phone numbers and email addresses in the screenshot. It's pretty accurate and puts a black bar over sensitive information, which is much safer than blurring phone numbers and email addresses.

Setting up an elaborate screenshot on your PC can be frustrating since Snipping Tool takes the screenshot instantly by default. In these instances, you can set a delay of three to 10 seconds before you capture the screen. If you have the Snipping Tool open, right-click its icon in the taskbar to quickly take a timed screenshot. Three buttons let you take a screenshot in three, five, or 10 seconds. You can also set up the Snipping Tool to always add a delay before capturing a screenshot. Open the app, and click the camera icon in the toolbar. Then, click the timer icon in the toolbar, and select the delay you wish to add.

When my friends or family members call for help with tech issues, I often send them a screencast with commentary to show how to fix the issue. In Snipping Tool, you can toggle a setting to include microphone audio by default when you record the screen. This lets me record my voice while I'm demonstrating how to solve the problem, and I use the mouse pointer to highlight what to click. Once you set up Snipping Tool to record your audio by default for screen recordings, this process hardly takes any time. Open Snipping Tool in your PC, and click the three-dots icon in the top-right corner. Select Settings, and enable Include microphone input by default when a screen recording starts.

When you capture screenshots, you can make Snipping Tool automatically add a solid color border to each image. This is great for posting to social media, as it makes screenshots look uniform and fit your aesthetic. Go to Snipping Tool settings and enable Add border to each screenshot. Select the Color block to pick the color you want for the border, and use the Thickness slider to adjust the width of the border.

The Freeform tool lets you draw an area on the screen, and captures a screenshot of everything inside that area. You can draw any shape you like, and the tool automatically closes small gaps in the shape to complete the screenshot. I like the fact that the Freeform tool is forgiving enough to smooth out poorly drawn shapes, which means you don't necessarily need to have steady hands to capture useful screenshots. To use this tool, open Snipping Tool, and click the camera icon in the toolbar. Next, select the rectangle icon, and choose Freeform. When you take the next screenshot, Snipping Tool will let you draw an irregular shape on the screen.

If you disable auto-save for screenshots, it directly copies screenshots to the clipboard. You can then make edits and send them to the app you need, or hit the save button to store the edited screenshots. This stops screenshots from piling up and adding to the clutter on your hard drive. I only need to save around one in 10 screenshots I capture, which makes this particularly useful for me. To try it out, go to Snipping Tool settings and disable Automatically save original screenshots.

Snipping Tool has a "Shapes" option, which is meant to hide people's faces from images or screenshots. Here's how it works: Once you open an image in Snipping Tool, you'll see a bunch of editing tools in the toolbar. Select the Shapes tool, which is next to the Eraser tool, and you'll see a series of options. Select the Emoji tool to add an emoticon over faces. Alternatively, you can select the Square or Oval tools, but be sure to use the color fill option to hide private information thoroughly. Select Fill, and choose a color. You can also disable the Outline if you wish to, as it adds a border to the shape you draw on the screenshot. Then, you can draw a rectangle, square, circle, or an oval on the screenshot, and you'll find a solid color block that can hide sensitive information.

Snipping Tool has a reverse image search feature that uses Bing to locate objects, places, or elements from your screenshots or images. You can use this to identify subjects in an image, or to check if a scammer has copied a profile picture from a different person's profile. To use this feature, open an image in Snipping Tool, and click the three dots in the top-right corner of the app. Select Visual Search with Bing, and it will open Bing's reverse image search results in your default browser.

title: 10 Hacks Every Google Sheets User Should Know
description: Spreadsheets don't have to be scary.
fullText:
If you don't spend hours every day working in spreadsheets, you may know only the basics of what Google Sheets can do: add, subtract, and sort data. But Sheets has a lot of powerful features that make data management simpler for even the casual user. Here are 10 hidden Google Sheets tricks everyone should know.

One of the best features of Sheets and other Google Workspace apps is that collaborators can make and view changes in real time. In some cases, though, you may not want to share your live spreadsheet, instead providing a clean copy or a downloadable CSV. With editable sharing links, you don't need to make copies or export manually. Simply replace /edit at the end of the link with /copy (for a clean duplicate) or either /export?format=pdf or /export?format=csv (for file downloads).

When you want collaborators to review a specific part of a large dataset, you don't need to provide a cell number or range for them to find manually. Instead, send them a link directly to an individual cell or cell block. Highlight the cell or cell range, right-click, and select View more cell actions > Get a link to this cell/range. The link will be copied to your clipboard so it can be easily shared.

Sheets has powerful data visualization features, but if all you need is a simple trend line, you can do that within a cell for an at-a-glance look at data over time. This also keeps your spreadsheet clean, so you don't have multiple charts and graphs overlaying the rest of your data. Type =SPARKLINE into a cell, select your range, and hit Enter.

Conditional formatting applies colors to your cells based on specific rules—for example, color-coding project statuses or deadlines based on due dates or turning negative currency amounts red while positive amounts display green. An extra layer of conditional formatting is custom gradients, which shades values based on a scale so you can see high and low ends of the range at a glance. To set this up, go to Format > Conditional formatting > Color scale and select the cell range, min and max values, and color gradient. Then press Done.

Smart Chips are interactive, clickable elements in Google Workspace that allow you to tag contributors, link files, insert tables or status dropdowns, or quickly add dates and emojis to your spreadsheet. When you add a Drive file, for example, clicking the cell will pull up a preview of and link to the document, which is far cleaner than copying and pasting the full URL. Simply type "@" into any cell to pull up the Smart Chip menu.

While Sheets doesn't have the same native text substitution feature as Docs (allowing you to set up shortcuts that automatically turn into longer text), there is a workaround using dropdowns. This way, you can quickly add longer inputs that you frequently find yourself typing out and formatting, such as addresses, phone numbers, category labels, and brand names. Go to Insert > Dropdown and enter the text you want to appear in the Option box. You can add multiple choices and color code them as well. (Alternatively, you can use the Smart Chip hack above and select Dropdown from the menu.)

Another text tweak in Sheets and across Workspace is the personal dictionary, which keeps Google from marking words as spelling errors. Add brand-specific terms, names, and other commonly used words and phrases via Tools > Spelling > Personal dictionary.

If you want to pull publicly available data into your spreadsheet but don't want to go through the potentially tedious process of copying, pasting, and reformatting, use the IMPORTHTML command to have Sheets do all of that for you. Paste =IMPORTHTML("url", "query", "index") and fill in the URL of the page you want to pull from, whether it's a "table" or "list" in the query field, and the table number on the live page. The data refreshes each time you open or refresh your spreadsheet, so you don't have to update them manually. Note that this function only works on public websites that don't require a login to access.

If you do need to import raw data from external sources (like CSVs) into your spreadsheet, Sheets can take care of some of the cleanup, so you don't have to manually remove duplicates from a huge dataset. Go to Data > Data Cleanup and select from Remove duplicates, Trim whitespace, or Cleanup suggestions.

Google Forms feed responses into Sheets, but you can also go in reverse and link a new form to your existing spreadsheet. For example, within your master budget spreadsheet, you can create a new tab for each month, and then use a Google Form with basic questions like transaction date, amount, and expense type to submit charges that autopopulate back to that tab instead of dealing in the spreadsheet directly. Go to Tools > Create a new form. This will pull up a form response tab in your spreadsheet (which can be renamed for the specific month) and an editable Google Form. Note that you'll need to publish the form in order to use it. If you have Workspace AI features, you can also have AI generate the form for you.

Sheets has a built-in Google Translate function, which allows you to convert text from one language to another without copying and pasting into another tool. Use this when you travel to create a dynamic, side-by-side phrase dictionary or apply it to a Google Form feedback sheet that receives inputs in multiple languages. Paste the command =GOOGLETRANSLATE(cell, "auto", "target_language") in which "auto" is the current language ("en" for English, for example). Then, highlight and drag across the row or down the column as needed.

title: AI Bots Can Steal Your Login Credentials, but You Can Protect Yourself
description: AI is getting better at finding things—including your passwords.
fullText:
AI agents are always getting better at finding things, which includes sensitive information like your passwords, financial information, and API secrets if they are left exposed in obvious places. You may have been following the recent news coverage on OpenAI’s rogue agent attacking the Hugging Face servers during an evaluation. But you may not have noticed that tucked in OpenAI’s public disclosure on the hack is an admission that its AI models have been targeting publicly exposed online credentials even before this incident. The day after OpenAI’s disclosure, Anthropic came forward with a report of similar incidents with multiple Claude models dating as far back as April of this year.

A few years ago, Security Magazine reported on a study that found up to 24 billion username and password combinations circulating on the dark web in 2022. This doesn’t even begin to account for all the exposed tokens, secrets, and API keys sitting in public repositories across GitHub or Hugging Face. All of this information is accessible to anyone with an internet connection—but thanks to the processing power of agentic AI, they can now be discovered and executed at record speed.

Info stealers who specialize in this kind of breaching regularly use AI-powered tools to scrape publicly exposed user credentials. Now—as we have just seen with OpenAI—apparently large language models can even find and use these exposed logins of their own volition. So how does one protect their user accounts on online platforms? First, you have to see if your credentials have been exposed. Then you have to take immediate steps to remediate them.

According to OpenAI, one of its GPT-5.6 Sol agents was being evaluated on a platform called ExploitGym, which benchmarks large language models by asking them to write proof-of-concept security exploits for known vulnerabilities. Normally, ExploitGym is designed to be a closed ecosystem for proof-of-concept testing only, and AI agents shouldn’t have access to the internet while being evaluated.

But this agent found a zero-day vulnerability in a package registry tool called Artifactory, then used it to gain access to the web. From there, the OpenAI agent gained access to Hugging Face’s company systems using publicly exposed credentials across four separate services. It went on to spend two days inside the company’s internal systems, managed to secure root access to several production servers, and even enrolled 181 attacker-controlled devices into Hugging Face’s corporate network.

As for how the AI agent was able to get past the model’s usual safeguards, OpenAI noted that due to the nature of the ExploitGym evaluation, the agent was operating on instructions that reduced cyber refusals to successfully evaluate the model. OpenAI’s disclosure notes that this issue isn’t limited to Hugging Face: It’s since found instances where its agents found and used leaked credentials across different platforms. Now the AI company is collaborating with Hugging Face to uncover more details about the attack and prevent further instances like this one.

Following the OpenAI reveal, Anthropic issued a public notice announcing it had begun a large-scale review of its own cybersecurity transcripts, which had already revealed similar attacks aimed at three separate organizations on different occasions, including Hugging Face. The attacks involved a different Claude model each time: Opus 4.7, Mythos 5, and another undisclosed research model. Like the OpenAI Hugging Face breach, Anthropic’s attacks also involved AI agents escaping controlled test environments to gain internet access during model evaluations.

But in this case, Anthropic claims that the test environments each had a configuration error that left the Claude models with internet access, which was not part of the evaluation protocol. It seems they didn’t even need to uncover or target an exploit in the evaluation environment because the misconfiguration was already there.

While using AI to scrape for exposed data is a new problem, the data leaks themselves are not. However, agents make it faster and easier to find leaked credentials because they can go through a large amount of information at record time or even execute hacks on autopilot. There are a few common routes that AI-automated scraping usually happens through, all of it to do with one or another form of human mistake leading sensitive data to become accessible in the first place.

Right after a major data breach or cyber attack, dump files containing huge numbers of compromised usernames, passwords, emails, and other sensitive data end up on dark web forums and marketplaces. They are searchable and often openly accessible, which means agents can find them just as easily as a human attacker can.

In June 2026, a database with over 24 billion credentials just surfaced on an Elasticsearch cluster, cross-referenced with live vulnerabilities to make it easier for hackers to pick low-hanging targets. There was another major data breach that led to 16 billion leaked credentials in mid-2025.

Developers often commit API keys, tokens, and passwords to public coding repositories by mistake, especially when they’re in a rush or using vibe coding tools for assistance. If a human being were to scroll GitHub or Hugging Face, they wouldn’t see these credentials out in the open. But if any hacker or AI agent decides to peek underneath for the source code, those credentials are easily reachable. In 2023, Lasso Security uncovered more than 1,500 exposed API keys on Hugging Face, many of which belonged to major tech companies like Meta and Google.

Even if your credentials aren’t exposed in advance, prompt injection has made it incredibly easy to break into someone’s device and scrape for any user credentials and logged-in accounts within reach. Hackers can manipulate AI agents with access to your local storage to search for unprotected passwords and browser session cookies, which can then be fed remotely to attackers who can use them to breach your private accounts. If your AI agent has access to your local device and web browser, you’re especially vulnerable. In some cases, a remote hacker may fully take over your system and quietly run surveillance without you even realizing.

You may not even know if your credentials end up on a public database or open source code file, or if you’re the subject of a prompt injection attempt right now, unless you use specific tools and strategies to monitor your data leakage. Based on the three exposure points we discussed earlier, here are some tools and strategies that work for identifying and plugging potential leaks:

Have I Been Pwned maintains a continuously updated library of known info steals and data breaches. They pulled 56 million email addresses from stealer logs in a single batch in June 2026 alone. It’s also entirely searchable and free to use.

You can search by either email address or password to see if your credentials are compromised from a recent data leak. If you’d like to search multiple email addresses across a shared domain that you own, you can get a paid subscription for as little as $4.39 per month. This also gives you access to their API, along with a live monitoring service that constantly checks your domain against new breaches as they happen.

If you write code, own a website, or maintain any public repositories, there’s a good chance that private credentials like passwords or tokens may end up in your public-facing source code files due to human error or technical issues.

You can run free tools like TruffleHog or Gitleaks against your public repositories, cloud storage systems, wikis, logs, and databases to scan for exposed secrets. They can alert you even if an exposed credential was removed from your live repository but still exists in a publicly accessible version history.

If you own a WordPress site with lots of plugins or themes, you can find similar vulnerabilities using WPScan. GitHub repositories also have access to their own built-in secret scanning tool, which can scan your repos for compromised API keys in a few clicks.

Prompt injection attacks don’t rely on publicly available or exposed credentials but instead target the AI agents that have access to your devices and applications. For users who rely on platforms like ChatGPT Work, Claude Cowork, Microsoft Copilot, etc., you should regularly review your AI platform to see what files and services it has access to. Generally speaking, it’s always better to restrict privileged access unless the specific job demands it, so your agent can’t just poke around in your file systems or hand over access to connected online platforms that you have accounts with.

Another thing you should do is review your AI platform’s activity logs to make sure it’s not doing anything that you haven’t authorized, like accessing folders on its own or exchanging data with sources you haven’t approved. If you see anything suspicious, revoke permissions immediately to avoid further damage and change your compromised account credentials.

If running these checks triggered a detection, you need to take immediate action to prevent your accounts from being compromised any further. Here’s what to do if you realize you might be exposed to AI scraping.

If you suspect a password has been compromised, either through public data leaks or prompt injection attacks targeting your device, the first course of action is to log into your account and reset that password. You can use a random password generator to create one that’s hard to guess, ideally with a mix of numbers and symbols along with text.

Once the password has been reset, look for an option that says something along the lines of “log out of all sessions.” If not, see if your account has a “manage devices” option for individually managing any signed-in device sessions. Make sure that you’re logged out of every device and session, so that attackers don’t retain access in case they have already breached your account.

If your compromised data includes any API keys, tokens, secrets, or other developer credentials in publicly accessible source code, don’t wait until a cyber attack occurs to reset them. It’s best to assume that an attack is likely if it’s not already taken place, so replace your credentials with new ones at once.

But don’t stop there. Search every bit of your live code, CI/CD logs, chat exports, and shared documents and files to see if the same key or token has been reused elsewhere. If it has, reset each instance of the leaked credential so that attackers can’t run a brute-force attack against all your accounts using the compromised secret.

Two-factor authentication (2FA) is a fundamental security stopgap that prevents most account takeover attempts during cyber attacks. Even if a hacker manages to secure a compromised password, they can’t actually get into your accounts unless they also have access to the one-time code from your authenticator app or your private security key.

For even better security, avoid using SMS authentication when enabling 2FA. SMS messages can be easily intercepted through SIM-swapping, which is less of an issue if it’s just your password that’s been compromised but a much bigger problem if your accounts end up in a massive data dump after a breach at a major company.

Authenticator apps like Google Authenticator, Bitwarden, 2FAS, Authy, etc. offer much better security because they’re locked to your specific device and account. Physical security keys are also a great option that insulates you from all forms of digital attacks altogether since logging in requires access to a piece of physical hardware.

Even if that GitHub project is just for testing, hardcoding your secrets and tokens into a public repository will make it simple for agents to scrape your login credentials for attackers. Instead of pasting your API keys directly into script files, use environment variables or dedicated secret managers.

AI agents or browsers like ChatGPT Work, Perplexity Comet, Dia, or Claude Cowork live directly on your desktop and execute tasks like coding, file management, and web browsing autonomously. But if you give them blanket access to your whole device, prompt injection attacks can easily steal files that store your credentials or active cookie sessions from logged-in accounts in your browser.

Relegate your AI agent’s access permissions to a single controlled file system or folder. For everything else, approve requests on a per-task basis to avoid automatic prompt injection attacks from executing.

When you stop using online accounts but don’t actively delete or decommission them, they continue to sit in a company database along with your old password, payment details, and other personal information. These dormant accounts on online platforms are a favorite target for AI-augmented info stealers, who find them easier to exploit due to reduced security measures and outdated authentication.

When you stop using an account, make sure to use the platform’s built-in "close account" or "delete account" option to permanently remove your information from their database. If these options aren’t available in the platform’s UI itself, it might be worth shooting an email to their customer support team to get the account decommissioned, even if that feels like a bit of extra hassle.

Some companies will still keep your data on file for compliance reasons for a set period after decommissioning the account, but that’s usually not an indefinite amount of time, and your account won’t be sitting open to exploitation in the meantime.

title: Murderer told mum and former prison officer to move tens of thousands of pounds
description: David Braddon was jailed for life, with a minimum term of 20 years, for killing Conner Marshall in 2015.
fullText:
A convicted murderer will have to serve an extra three-and-a-half years for carrying out further crimes behind bars.

David Braddon, 38, was jailed for life with a minimum term of 20 years for killing 18-year-old Conner Marshall, from Barry, at Trecco Bay caravan park in Porthcawl, Bridgend, on 8 March 2015.

Earlier this year, he admitted having a mobile phone in prison which he used to direct three women to move tens of thousands of pounds between bank accounts.

Those women were Braddon's mother Karen Graham, 57, along with his former partner Gemma Phillips, 41, and former probationary prison officer Claire Jones, 38.

The transactions totalled more than £50,000, but ranged from £4 to £4,175, Cardiff Crown Court heard.

The money was moved between bank accounts belonging to 59 people including the relatives of 32 prisoners at HMPs Parc, Eastwood Park, Hewell and Oakwood.

The offences came to light when a prison officer at HMP Parc was sent a message on Facebook telling him to go to a specific cell to meet an inmate.

He refused to comply and passed the details on to prison authorities and the police.

Jones was arrested and her phone was seized, with investigators finding the messages.

She later admitted setting up a Monzo bank account which was used, in effect, to launder money, but said she felt "under pressure" to engage in Braddon's activities.

Conner's mother, Nadine Marshall, found out about Braddon's further offending when she read a news article.

Judge Tracey Lloyd-Clarke agreed Nadine could read a personal statement to the court about the impact this has had, even though she was not directly a victim of the offences.

They were, however, committed by Braddon while he was serving a sentence for a crime where she was a victim.

Nadine fought back tears as she read her statement to the court.

"My stomach dropped," she said, adding: "I had butterflies and felt nauseous, and had flashbacks of my son in the neck brace."

She said the news had left her feeling upset and immediately fearful, with Braddon's police custody photo bringing back painful memories.

"That picture of him was 11 years ago when he murdered my son, and all of those horrific memories came flooding back."

Nadine said she was on medication after being diagnosed with complex post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).

She said on the morning she saw the news she "went through every emotion possible... from shock, emotional distress, tearful, vulnerable, anxious to being angry".

Braddon shouted from the dock: "I'm sorry. I truly am sorry. I am."

Lloyd-Clarke sentenced Braddon to three years and seven months for possessing a phone in prison and for the acquisition, use or control of criminal property, namely money.

She told him that it would be added to the end of the minimum term he was already serving.

Jones and Griffiths were both sentenced to two years and nine months for their roles in Braddon's crimes.

Graham was given a sentence of one year and six months suspended for two years, and will have to carry out 20 days' rehabilitation.

title: FCC chairman defends actions against ABC, says broadcasters must operate 'in the public interest'
description: Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr on Friday defended his agency’s recent actions against ABC, saying broadcasters have a duty to “operate in the public interest” and the FCC is m...
fullText:
Federal Communications Commission Chairman Brendan Carr on Friday defended his agency's recent actions against ABC, saying broadcasters have a duty to "operate in the public interest" and the FCC is merely trying to restore that standard.

Broadcasters like ABC, Carr said in an interview on the Fox Business Network, "struck a deal with the American people. You broadcasters get subsidized access, free access to a valuable public resource, the airwaves, worth billions of dollars. In exchange, you have to operate in the public interest."

"Look, as a country, we should have a trusted, respected news media, and we're not there," Carr told anchor Maria Bartiromo. "So I hope more broadcasters return to their public interest obligations."

The remarks came a day after ABC, issuing another salvo in an ever-escalating battle with President Donald Trump's FCC, again accused the agency of a brazen attempt to chill its constitutionally protected free speech — and by extension, that of every media outlet in the country.

ABC accused the agency of retaliating against it simply because it doesn't like the political content of ABC's shows.

The network's new comments came in its latest filing to the agency, expressing its formal opposition to the FCC's early review, launched in April, of eight ABC local broadcast licenses well before they expire.

"There is no question why the Commission is singling out these eight stations," the filing said. "Each is owned by ABC, and the Administration has openly and repeatedly called for the revocation of ABC's licenses, because it dislikes the content and viewpoints expressed on ABC network programs."

"The retaliation against ABC is a signal to every media company in the country," it continued. "Accommodate the Administration's view of what news coverage should look like or pay the price. … The tools vary; the objective does not: a media industry too fearful of official reprisal to report the news freely. "

The license review is only one part of a long-simmering confrontation between ABC and the FCC. The network is also battling Carr's efforts to make "The View," a talk show whose hosts and guests have frequently angered Trump, subject to equal-time rules — a question ABC says the agency itself resolved more than two decades ago.

The rules require granting equal airtime to competing candidates for office. Bona fide news programs are exempt. The FCC qualified the show as such in a 2002 decision.

Trump has also repeatedly called for late-night host Jimmy Kimmel to be fired.

When the FCC launched its early review of ABC's licenses in April, it came amid a fight with Kimmel over a joke that offended Trump. The agency, however, cited diversity, equity and inclusion practices at the company, and Carr brought them up in the Fox interview.

Operating in the public interest, he said, "means you can't run news distortions, broadcast hoax. You can't be engaging in this invidious form of DEI discrimination." He did not elaborate.

In its filing Thursday, ABC referred to over 140,000 comments from viewers, part of the public comment period on the issue, posted to the FCC website — more than 95% of which it said were supportive of ABC's position.

"The outpouring of support for the Stations has been unprecedented for a license renewal proceeding," it said. "These supporters span the ideological spectrum but share a fundamental commitment to free speech and press freedom."

In its lengthy filing, ABC also noted how rare it is that the FCC would call for early license renewal applications.

"Until the day before the Commission took this step, it had not called for license renewal applications ahead of schedule for more than fifty years," ABC said. "The Commission's departure from those norms lays bare what is really going on: the Administration is retaliating against ABC for the exercise of its First Amendment rights.

"That alone should stop these proceedings in their tracks."

Jocelyn Noveck covers the intersection of media and entertainment for The Associated Press.

title: Beever-Jones ready to 'conquer' new season after injury troubles last term
description: Chelsea and England forward Aggie Beever-Jones had her "hardest" season in 2025-26 and she had a big decision to make about her future when it ended.
fullText:
England forward Aggie Beever-Jones had her "hardest" season in 2025-26 and when it ended, she had a big decision to make about her future.

Successive ankle injuries meant lengthy periods out of action as Chelsea's title defence faltered, all while her contract was running down.

But despite interest from other Women's Super League clubs, the 23-year-old signed a new four-year deal at Chelsea and intends to play a key role this season as the Blues try to bounce back from a disappointing campaign.

"I look at my career at Chelsea so far and I had quite a successful start," she told BBC Sport.

"Last year, as a club, it was probably our hardest season. We got one trophy, which isn't up to our standards.

"Personally, it was the toughest year with injuries. It put me on the sidelines quite a bit and I really struggled getting consistency back.

"I spent a lot of time this summer recovering to conquer this season and I'm really delighted to have signed a new contract. It definitely felt like the right thing."

Beever-Jones used the summer off to recover and travel, visiting Copenhagen and Los Angeles before grabbing a ticket to watch the men's World Cup final.

In that time, she learned to prioritise her body - something she had not thought about as much previously because of her rapid success and consistent goalscoring form.

Successful loan spells at Bristol City and Everton were followed by 11 goals for Chelsea in the 2023-24 season, finishing with the best minutes-per-goal ratio in the WSL and earning an England call-up.

The season after continued in a similar vein. She was Chelsea's top scorer on the way to an unbeaten domestic treble, and capped by winning Euro 2025 with England.

But last season she learned a harsh lesson, only once completing a full game after Christmas while Manchester City ended Chelsea's six-year stranglehold on the WSL.

"It was extremely tough - it was the first big injury I had," Beever-Jones said of her ankle issues.

"I'm never going to go off the pitch unless I'm in absolute agony. There were a few times where I wanted to carry on pushing and my body was not ready and I really struggled with that.

"The mental side isn't always spoken about enough. My job is to be a footballer and as soon as that's taken away from me, I feel empty.

"It's hard to fill that void. You come to training and you try to put on a brave face but you do feel a little bit isolated.

"There were some dark times but I think that's all part of the journey that you need to go on to really appreciate the good times."

Beever-Jones says she feels "stronger" after that challenging period and is ready to fight for a consistent starting role at Chelsea.

She also has her mind on the Women's World Cup next year and to catch England manager Sarina Wiegman's eye as the Lionesses attempt to reach a fourth successive major final.

The striker has netted seven goals in 16 England appearances, including a memorable first-half hat-trick against Portugal at Wembley in 2025.

However, she has often found herself below Alessia Russo and, at Euro 2025, Michelle Agyemang in the pecking order - so is this a crucial season for Beever-Jones?

"That's why I was so gaffed about last year," she said. "[The World Cup is] my ambition and I hope I can get there, but I've just got to take each day as it comes."

Beever-Jones reminded WSL fans of her abilities with a starring role at the World Sevens in May where she scored six goals, including Chelsea's winner in the final against Manchester United.

"The World Sevens tournament was such a good time for me. It was finally when I felt back at full fitness and I was ready to go," she added.

"It was a shame that the season came to an end then but that was me in my flow state - when I'm happy, I'm enjoying it and I'm not playing in pain.

"Obviously it's a really big year with the World Cup and I just hope I can help to grow the game and Chelsea can dominate domestically and in Europe."

Clubs lower down the WSL such as London City Lionesses, Tottenham and Brighton have all made big investments in their playing squads this summer.

At the top end, champions Manchester City have added England internationals Beth Mead and Niamh Charles - from Chelsea - while Arsenal have also strengthened.

However, prior to last season's disappointment, Chelsea had won six successive WSL titles, while they have been in every Women's League Cup final since 2019 and have reached the semi-finals of the Women's Champions League in three of the past four campaigns.

So is it foolish to write them off this season?

"There's been a lot of noise around Chelsea. Other teams are signing but you look at our squad and I'd still say we have incredible, world-class players," said Beever-Jones.

"We've brought in Katie McCabe, Melvine Malard, Manaka Matsukubo - world-class players who have already really impressed.

"We're doing the work behind the scenes that doesn't always get put out in the media. I'm confident within the team we share that common goal.

"I believe we'll show that when we need to. I have every faith that it will be us that wins and that we'll work hard."

title: Ancient mammoth remains and a Nazi shipwreck: Europe’s shrinking rivers reveal past relics
description: The continent’s summer of extraordinary heat and drought has pushed some of its rivers to record lows, revealing long submerged relics from ancient bones to century-old shipwrecks.
fullText:
Europe's summer of extraordinary heat and drought has pushed some of its rivers to record lows, revealing long-submerged relics from ancient bones to century-old shipwrecks.

The remains of what's believed to be an ancient mammoth were discovered Wednesday on the newly exposed riverbed of the Danube in northern Bulgaria, after the river plunged to record lows.

The director of the Regional History Museum in the nearby town of Ruse said the discovery consists of a lower jaw, two tusks and potentially a rib, according to Reuters, citing local media reports. The bones will now be tested to confirm the find.

The Danube also runs through Croatia, where receding water has revealed the skeleton of a cargo ship called the Fulton, which was transporting coal down the river when it sank in 1937.

And in Serbia, the shrunken river has exposed the remains of a sunken Nazi warship.

This summer, Europe has been roiled by a succession of extreme, record-breaking heat waves, which scientists are clear have been made more intense by the human-driven climate crisis. Not has the hot, dry weather primed the land for the destructive wildfires sweeping through the continent, but it's also putting immense pressure on its water sources.

Gushing rivers have shrunk to a trickle, vast tracts of desiccated riverbed now lie exposed, and the crisis is affecting everything from shipping and tourism to water availability and energy generation.

Parts of the Danube, Europe's second-largest river which winds through 10 countries, have shrunk to unprecedented lows.

In Budapest, the capital of Hungary, the national water authority measured a water level in the Danube of 9 inches on Wednesday, shattering the previous record low of 13 inches set in 2013, according to the Associated Press. Little relief is on the horizon, with no significant rain forecast for the region over the next few days.

It's having a serious effect on energy. Hungary is set to close a nuclear plant that produces nearly half the country's electricity, potentially for weeks.

"For the first time in 44 years, the entire Paks Nuclear Power Plant will be completely shut down due to the record-low water level of the Danube. An energy crisis situation may arise from Monday" Prime Minister Peter Magyar said Thursday in a post on X. Water from the Danube is used to cool the facility.

Ships are being disrupted, with cargo ships having to significantly reduce their loads in order to avoid getting stuck, making shipping much slower and more expensive.

Shrunken rivers are also affecting tourism, forcing some river cruises to cancel or alter services. A cruise ship ran aground on a sandbank in the Danube in Bulgaria Tuesday.

Other rivers are suffering across the continent. Lake Brenets on the border between Switzerland and France, which is a big tourist draw, has all but dried up as water levels have dropped in the River Doubs which feeds it. Boats now lie stranded on the exposed lakebed.

Scientists warn Europe can expect heat and drought to only get more severe unless the world rapidly reduces the amount of oil, coal add gas it burns.

"The heat dries the soil, empties the rivers and drives up demand for water all at once. That is the fingerprint of a changing climate," said Hannah Cloke, Regius professor of meteorology and climate science at the University of Reading, in the UK

"Summers like this are becoming part of the ordinary range, and they will keep getting worse as long as we burn fossil fuels," she added. "That is the plain physics of it."

title: Massachusetts is close to giving doctors the final word on whether to perform late abortions
description: Massachusetts is on the way to giving doctors the final say on whether an abortion should be allowed late in pregnancy, a move expected to affect few cases but that supporters say is needed because ho...
fullText:
Massachusetts is on the way to giving doctors the final say on whether an abortion should be allowed late in pregnancy, a move expected to affect few cases but that supporters say is needed because hospitals are now turning away women they should be serving.

The state Senate adopted the measure Friday, sending it to Democratic Gov. Maura Healey, who has signed other laws strengthening abortion rights.

Under current Massachusetts law, abortion is legal for the first 24 weeks of pregnancy. It is allowed after that only if a physician using best medical judgment says it is necessary to preserve the life, physical or mental health of the woman, because of a lethal fetal anomaly or diagnosis or because the fetus wouldn't likely survive outside the uterus.

State Rep. Christine Barber said that under that framework, hospitals turned away some women for abortions late in pregnancy, even in a case where a fetus had a stroke and was determined to be unlikely to survive.

The new law would take out the list of specific reasons and say simply that it would be allowed "based on the professional judgment of the physician."

Opponents say that it would allow abortion until birth — even on healthy fetuses — and that later abortions are more complex and risky for the women.

"While this legislation prioritizes access, it does not prioritize a woman's safety," Myrna Maloney Flynn, president of Massachusetts Citizens for Life, said in a video encouraging supporters to tell lawmakers to reject the bill.

If Healey signs it, the law would be the latest change to a U.S. abortion landscape that received a shock four years ago after a Supreme Court ruling that overturned Roe v. Wade and allowed states to enforce abortion bans.

Some already had bans on the books as they waited for permission to enforce them, and others adopted bans or restrictions after the ruling. Currently, 13 states are enforcing bans abortion at all stages of pregnancy, with some exceptions. Another four bar it after about six weeks of pregnancy — which is often before women realize they are pregnant.

Several Democratic-controlled states have moved the other way, adding laws that seek to protect medical providers from prosecution for providing abortion to patients in other states. Massachusetts is among the states that has gone farthest, with a shield law that applies to those who prescribe abortion bills via telehealth to women in states where abortion is banned. Anti-abortion officials in Louisiana and Texas are testing those protections.

Most abortion-related state laws adopted this year have not made for major changes on when or how abortion is allowed.

For instance, a new Colorado law requires colleges that have student health centers to provide abortion pills for students starting in August 2027. Private schools that say it conflicts would their religious beliefs would be exempt.

A new Oklahoma law makes it a felony to buy or sell those pills for the purpose of an unlawful abortion for someone else.

title: England's Toprak wins judo gold with golden score
description: England judoka Acelya Toprak overcomes India's Yamini Mourya in the women's -57kg final to win gold at the Commonwealth Games.
fullText:
England's Acelya Toprak overcame India's Yamini Mourya in the women's -57kg judo final to win the gold medal at the Commonwealth Games.

In an exhausting bout that went to golden score and lasted almost seven minutes, Toprak eventually forced Mourya into a third shido to claim victory.

The 28-year-old had won silver in 2022 but managed to go one better this time around in Glasgow.

"My last Commonwealth Games went exactly the same way. In the final it was two shidos each, we were into four-and-a-half minutes of extra time and I made that one misstep, over-stretched and got caught," Toprak told BBC Sport.

"So I'm very happy that this time I didn't do that, because that's shattering, that hurts.

"All you're thinking about is get up and go again, get up and go again, and then after I was like 'I like a golden score in the finals, don't I?'

"You're exhausted, someone's trying to throw you on your head for eight minutes and you've just got to get up and go again."

It was an excellent night for England's judo athletes with all five who were in medal contention winning their matches.

Lele Nairne, who was beaten by Toprak in the women's -57kg semi-final, won bronze by ippon with an emphatic throw to the mat to defeat Ghanaian 17-year-old Frema Agyei within just 28 seconds.

"I love throwing people like that," Nairne, 28, said after her victory.

"I love it. It's a bittersweet symphony. Birmingham [2022] was tragic, I lost to a good friend in the bronze medal match, so I wanted to redeem myself.

"I wanted a medal, I wanted a gold, but just to get a medal, I'm absolutely over the moon."

Tatum Keen - Nairne's training partner at Bradley Stoke Judo Club in Bristol - also won bronze in the women's -52kg category.

And in the men's judo, 20-year-old Charlie Ayre and Michael Fryer, 26, claimed bronze in their respective -60kg and -66kg events.

title: Morris succeeds in gold pursuit but misses out on scratch medal
description: Welsh cyclist Anna Morris claims Commonwealth Games gold in the 4000m individual pursuit final in Glasgow by defeating England's Josie Knight.
fullText:
Welsh cyclist Anna Morris claimed Commonwealth Games gold in the 4,000m individual pursuit final in Glasgow before appearing to follow it up an hour later with a silver in the scratch before she was relegated off the podium.

Morris defeated England's Josie Knight in the pursuit final and claimed her gold medal on the podium.

She then rushed off for a scratch race that started 10 minutes later and eventually finished behind Australian winner Georgia Baker but was then demoted from the podium.

There was a rivalry between these Great Britain team-mates Morris and Knight in the individual pursuit.

They rode alongside each other in the team pursuit squad that won Olympic bronze in Paris in 2024.

Morris, a qualified doctor, then defeated Knight in the world final of the 2025 individual pursuit final as she defended her title.

The battle lines had been drawn in the morning session when Knight recorded the fastest qualifying time of 4:25.719, with Morris just outside in 4:25.817.

But Morris produced a commanding performance in the final to clinch gold in a time of 4:24:272.

This was the first time the event had been held over 4,000m in the Commonwealth Games having previously been a 3,000m contest.

Morris continued her remarkable evening by competing alongside Welsh riders Megan Barker and Carys Lloyd in the scratch and somehow still had the strength to finish second before her disappointment followed.

Morris was relegated for entering the sprinter's lane when her New Zealand opponent was already there.

title: England equal best boxing haul at Commonwealths
description: England equal their best ever boxing results at a Commonwealth Games, with seven reaching the finals and 10 claiming a medal.
fullText:
England's boxers equalled their best ever performance at a Commonwealth Games after seven fighters won through to Saturday's finals.

Dorset's Ruby White, dubbed the 'Pocket Rocket', was the standout performer, with the 19-year-old claiming the 68th consecutive win of her senior career to reach her first Commonwealth final.

England had already matched their best medal tally, set in Edinburgh in 1986, with 10 boxers reaching Friday's semi-finals to guarantee at least a bronze medal.

But with seven out of those 10 going on to clinch victory, England also equalled their record for boxing finalists at a Commonwealth Games - set in 1986 and matched at Gold Coast in 2018.

White was joined in the finals by Chantelle Reid and Sacha Hickey in the women's competition, while Isaac Okoh, Patris Mughalzai and Dimeji Shittu won through in the men's events and Damar Thomas took his place in the finals via a walkover.

However, England would need a 100% record in Saturday's finals to break their record of six boxing gold medals at a single Commonwealth Games, set in Australia eight years ago.

The finals are scheduled to take place from 11:00 to 19:30 BST on Saturday in Glasgow.

White produced the semi-finals' most eye-catching display to dismantle fellow teenager Mischa Araes inside two rounds.

After knocking the 18-year-old to the canvas at the end of the first round, the diminutive Dorset boxer forced Araes into two standing counts in the second round and the referee stopped the fight.

It continued her impressive winning run, which stretches back to more than 80 fights when including junior and youth bouts.

"I wanted to be in there for the full three minutes, I was enjoying it so much," she said.

"I couldn't ask for better. I'm a little bit lost for words, but the job is not done yet. I've got to bring that gold medal home."

White is scheduled to fight Sakshi Chaudhary - one of 10 Indian boxers to reach the finals - in the women's 51kg final at 16:30 BST on Saturday, and she knows exactly how she will prepare for the biggest fight of her burgeoning amateur career.

"I'm going to give my mum a big fat cuddle," she said. "And then I'm going to have an early night and get a steak before bed, that's my good luck charm."

White was the only England fighter to reach the finals in the evening session, with both Lucy Kings-Wheatley and Mary Kate Smith falling to narrow defeats.

Kings-Wheatley and Smith will pick up bronze medals, as will Lauren Mackie, who lost to Canada's Scarlett Delgado in the morning session.

But the rest of England's 10 semi-finalists will go on to fight for gold on Saturday.

Reid put in a superb display to comfortably make it past Australia's world number two Lekeisha Pergoliti in the women's 70kg semi-finals.

The 28-year-old world bronze medallist only recently returned to the ring after spending six years out with a degenerative back condition and says she is now looking forward to what she can do in the final.

She told TNT Sports: "I'm just going to try to keep getting these wins in. It's all good preparation for the Olympic Games [in Los Angeles in 2028]."

Okoh produced an equally disciplined performance to ease past Scotland's Robert McNulty in the men's heavyweight division (+90kg).

The 22-year-old quietened the home crowd in Glasgow, winning all three rounds before raising both gloves to his ears at the final bell as he waited for his unanimous win to be confirmed.

"They [McNulty's fans] have been hostile all week," said the Grays fighter. "I won on Tuesday and they came out and told me I was going to get knocked out, but there was no knocking out today. He got schooled."

In the morning session, Hickey overcame Australia's Eve Bryson 5-0 in the women's 65kg category and will take on Northern Ireland's Kaci Rock in Saturday's final.

Mughalzai will fight Australian Jacob Cassar for gold in the men's 65kg after powering past Zambia's Emmanuel Katema for a 4-1 win in his semi-final.

And Shittu enjoyed a comprehensive 5-0 victory over Australia's Paul Trainor to set up a final bout against India's Ankush Panghai.

Michaela Walsh and Jon McConnell will also fly the flag for Northern Ireland on Saturday, while Wales have two boxers in the finals - Connor Williams will take on England's Okoh in the 90kg category and Orlando Holley-Sotomi will fight McConnell in the men's 70kg final.

Meanwhile, a boxer from Tuvalu claimed her country's first ever Commonwealth Games medal without winning a fight.

Because there were only five entrants, Tarona Taafaki received a bye to the last four, meaning she was automatically guaranteed at least a bronze medal.

The 20-year-old lost her first and only fight in the women's 75kg division - which was a semi-final - to India's Lovlina Borgohain on Friday, losing every round on all three of the judges' cards.

Taafaki's coach and father, Badi Taafaki, says the population of the tiny Pacific island nation - at 10 square miles the fourth smallest in the world - will celebrate the medal and use it to highlight a climate change emergency.

"For the people of Tuvalu, this medal means everything," he said. "We're one of the smallest nations in the world, so a medal like this is hugely significant.

"If we can win medals, more people around the world will recognise Tuvalu and begin to understand the challenges we face because of climate change.

"It is very real for us. The coastal erosion is unbelievable, and the countdown is now measured in years, not decades."

title: Ruthless Wigan seize on Leigh errors to go second
description: Wigan make it ten wins in a row in all competitions as a careless Leigh are made to pay for their mistakes in the Battle of the Borough.
fullText:
Tries: Field, French, Eckersley, Hodkinson Goals: Smith 2

Wigan made it ten wins in a row in all competitions as careless Leigh were made to pay for their mistakes in an enthralling Battle of the Borough.

The Leopards, crushed 54-0 in the first meeting between the sides this season, dominated the opening half-hour and led at the break but self-destructed with a string of errors in the second period at Leigh Sports Village.

Wigan cashed in with four tries from Jai Field, Bevan French, Zach Eckersley and Noah Hodkinson in the space of 22 minutes either side of half-time to secure a comeback win that moves them up to second in Super League.

The defeat ended a run of five successive wins for Leigh who drop to fifth place in the standings.

Connor stars as pacesetting Leeds thrash Toulouse

Burgess scores 200th try as Hull KR beat Bradford

Leigh had Wigan on the back foot initially and after Adam Cook put them ahead with a straightforward penalty, the Leopards delivered the opening try in the 13th minute through Innes Senior. It was the wing's tenth try of the season from a slick assist by centre Andy Badrock, recalled from his loan with Widnes Vikings.

But they were left kicking themselves after switching off in defence to allow man of the match Field to show his scorching pace three minutes before half-time with a breakaway try.

It was quick thinking as well as quick feet from the Wigan full-back who raced 80 metres through a dozy Leigh defence after tapping a penalty.

Four minutes into the second half French gave Wigan the lead with Leigh again contributing to their own downfall. Jack Hughes' offload attempt to Gareth O'Brien went to ground allowing Wigan wing Hodkinson to pick up the loose ball and feed French who went over.

Another offload error from Lazarus Vaalepu in the 51st minute as French drove him back in the tackle saw Eckersley intercept and speed in from halfway for his 22nd try of the season.

Then a poor pass from Owen Trout presented Wigan with the position to strike just before the hour and they took it with some terrific handling as Hodkinson scored in the corner from Eckersley's tip pass.

Harry Smith added two goals for Wigan with Adam Keighran ruled out because of a groin injury.

Wigan's defence did the rest as the visitors closed out victory with room to spare.

Leigh head coach Adrian Lam told BBC Radio Merseyside:

"There were three tries from poor skill and a fourth one where we fell asleep at the wheel. It's not a whole team issue, it's just three or four moments that really hurt us.

"It was individuals that didn't nail skill at really big moments for us.

"I'm not going to get angry at the team. For 40 minutes I thought we were unbelievably good. I think we're very close to being very, very good and I'll hold onto that fact.

"I thought we dominated in most areas in that first half; we just have to put an 80-minute performance together."

Wigan head coach Matt Peet told BBC Radio Merseyside:

"I'm very proud. It is a tough place to come against a team that's flying. We had to overcome a bit of adversity. Leigh were excellent in the first half and we had to get a lot right to get the result.

"It had a play-off feel about it from minute one against a quality team who throw a lot at you.

"It will stand us in good stead. There are things that we can improve but the character of the team is very strong and defensively we looked very strong as well."

"It was a game-changing moment. He's got that capability and instinct and obviously his pace. He's a pleasure to watch."

title: 'Full heart, empty tank' - Eccles retires from boxing
description: The Welsh fighter confirmed she is hanging up her gloves before launching a verbal attack on "awful" people who tried to "end" her career.
fullText:
Three-time Commonwealth medallist Rosie Eccles has retired from boxing following defeat in Glasgow.

Eccles settled for bronze, to add to the gold and silver she won at previous Games, after a split-decision defeat in Friday's semi-final.

In an emotional interview after the narrow loss, the Welsh fighter confirmed she is hanging up her gloves before launching a verbal attack on "awful" people who tried to "end" her career.

"That's it for me now, I'm done," she told S4C.

"My heart's full but the tank is empty and I've got to accept that, otherwise I'll go on too long.

"I know I can contend for the Olympics, but I've got to put health first now.

"My life was nothing before boxing, so I will walk out of the sport with everything in my back pocket and on to the next stage of life."

Wales at the Commonwealth Games

The Caldicot light-middleweight, who turned 30 on the day she carried the Welsh flag at the opening ceremony in Glasgow, took up boxing aged 16 and joined the GB squad in 2018, the same year she won silver at the Gold Coast Games.

Her crowning moment was winning Commonwealth gold in Birmingham but that came between double Olympic heartache.

She missed out on Tokyo 2020 because of "horrendous" nerve damage linked to coronavirus before a controversial defeat at Paris 2024.

Since that devastating loss she has been hit with serious back and knee injuries before leaving the GB set-up in March.

"I'm so fortunate my team has got me back," she added.

"I'm gutted [to lose]. It's sad. It's my last time in the ring and that's what I'm most sad about."

In a highly charged post-fight interview, Eccles spoke about her recent struggles.

"This last year has been so tough," she told TNT Sports.

"I've talked about all the good people, but this last year there were some awful people - a small handful - who tried to end my career.

"I shouldn't say it but they nearly killed me last year and I'm stronger than them.

"Screw them. I have come back with the best people and [those other people] are on the fringes."

title: AC Milan and Italy great Baresi dies aged 66
description: AC Milan and Italy great Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, the Italian club announces.
fullText:
Franco Baresi has died at the age of 66, with AC Milan saying their former captain's "example and integrity will be forever etched into the club's DNA".

Baresi spent his entire 20-year playing career with the club from 1977 until he retired in 1997, winning six Serie A titles and three European Cups/Champions Leagues.

Regarded as one of the greatest defenders to play the game, Baresi captained Milan for 15 seasons, making 719 appearances and scoring 33 goals.

He was capped 81 times by Italy and was part of the squad which won the 1982 World Cup. He played and was captain in the 1994 final, which Italy lost to Brazil.

Baresi was made honorary president of Milan in 2020, and his number six shirt was retired when he finished his playing career.

Baresi formed part of one of European football's most celebrated defences alongside Paolo Maldini, Alessandro Costacurta and Mauro Tassotti.

He also lifted four Supercoppa Italianas, two European Super Cups and the Intercontinental Cup twice.

In the 1994 World Cup, he returned from a knee injury to play in the final and largely nullified the threat of Brazil's Romario and Bebeto in a 0-0 draw.

It was the first World Cup final to be decided by a shootout and Baresi missed the first penalty, with Brazil eventually winning it 3-2.

Baresi had surgery in August 2025 to remove a lung nodule, and his last public appearance was at the San Siro Stadium for the Winter Olympics opening ceremony in February.

In a statement on X, AC Milan wrote: "Milan is in tears following the passing of Franco Baresi. His example and integrity will be forever etched into the club's DNA, just as his iconic number 6 shirt is."

In a further post on the club's website,, external they added: "Announcing the loss of someone who embodied the heart and soul of AC Milan is incredibly difficult. But everyone at the club and all the Milanisti must live up to Franco Baresi's memory.

"In memory of Franco, we stand united, knowing he'll guide and push us throughout our Rossoneri journey. Forever. Because Baresi is forever."

Maldini, 58, who also spent his entire career at Milan, paid tribute to his former team-mate, writing on Instagram:, external "Today, I feel the same way I did whenever - for whatever reason - you couldn't take the field alongside us: how will we manage without our captain?

"You taught me to fight until my very last breath, and showed me the meaning of devotion to the jersey and the true value of leadership.

"You protected me when I was a child, guided me as a young man, and inspired me as an adult.

"You were the greatest footballer I ever had the honour of playing with."

Former Italy goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon shared memories of his debut for Parma competing against Baresi as a 17-year-old in 1995.

He wrote: "For a boy my age, finding myself on the field against champions like him was something incredible. From that day on, I had an even clearer understanding of what it meant to represent football with class, leadership and respect."

Inter Milan said:, external "Farewell to Franco Baresi, protagonist of the great clashes in the Milan derby and one of the figures who most defined the history of the rivalry.

"Captain, team man and flagbearer of AC Milan, he lived every match-up with Inter between competition and respect, within a challenge that wrote unforgettable pages of Italian soccer."

Inter Milan manager Cristian Chivu said Baresi's death "is a sad day for the whole world, he represented being one of the greats in the history of football".

Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni said Baresi "was not only one of the greatest champions in (Italian) sports history, but also an example of loyalty, seriousness, and dedication".

The head of the Italian football federation (FICG), Giovanni Malago, praised Baresi for the "romantic choice" of staying loyal to AC Milan throughout his career, "which rightfully made him enter the hearts of the fans and millions of Italians."

Everyone is hurting, it is a very sad day.

Franco Baresi is a legend in Italy, one of the last so-called 'flags' - a one-club player, a player who has only worn one shirt for his entire career.

After 15 years as AC Milan captain, his shirt had already been retired so no-one will ever wear the number six again - it shows how important he was for Milan, a symbol of the city.

At AC Milan they called him 'Piscinin' - it means a fragile, thin youngster in Milan dialect. That was his nickname when he started back in the 1970s and it was given to him by a famous Italian journalist called Gianni Brera.

He had a trial at Inter when he was 12 and his brother Beppe was already at the club, but they rejected him. He ended up at AC Milan that way. But even Inter are mourning, his value has been recognised by all opponents as he is a legend not only for AC Milan. Find me a fan who didn't like or recognise the value of Franco Baresi - it is not going to happen. That is how loved he was.

He played alongside some of the biggest champions, Marco van Basten, Paolo Maldini, Ruud Gullit, Frank Rijkaard and he was always at the same level. Baresi was one of the immortal AC Milan players.

He won three European Cups, but there were also some sad times - the World Cup in 1994 and the penalty miss. He couldn't play for much of the tournament given the injury he suffered at the beginning, but he made a speedy recovery to play a great game in the final against Brazil.

To then miss a penalty in the shootout was a very sad moment for the whole of Italy. But we have never been angry, because Franco Baresi was one of the pillars of the team and the fact he recovered to play in the final was simply inhuman.

And in 1989, he finished second in the Ballon d'Or to his team-mate Van Basten - back then, it was inconceivable a defender could win the Ballon d'Or, but Baresi got that close and deserved to win it for the player he was, the quality he had and all he represented - his leadership, importance, quality and his belonging to a club. He deserved that recognition.

title: The Premier League clubs fighting a World Cup hangover
description: Which Premier League clubs have carried the biggest World Cup workload?
fullText:
The Premier League season begins on 21 August - just 33 days after the World Cup final.

For some clubs, that leaves barely enough time to welcome players back from the mandatory three-week post-tournament break required under Fifa regulations, let alone integrate them into pre-season preparations.

Four Tottenham players were still involved on the final weekend of the tournament and may have little more than a week of training before the new campaign starts. Chelsea too were significantly affected.

And Manchester City and Arsenal have their own concerns after seeing more players than any other Premier League club reach the latter stages of the competition.

The World Cup may be over, but its impact on the Premier League is only just beginning.

Tottenham are among the clubs whose pre-season preparations have been most significantly impacted.

Cristian Romero and new signing Marcos Senesi reached the final with Argentina, while Pedro Porro helped Spain lift the trophy. Djed Spence remained with England until the third-place play-off on 18 July.

Assuming players take the minimum three weeks off under Fifa guidelines, the players who reached the final would not return until 9 August, while Spence's earliest return date would be 8 August.

That leaves them with around two weeks to reintegrate before their Premier League season begins at Brentford on 22 August.

However, Spurs confirmed that Senesi - who made two World Cup appearances after being a late call-up for Argentina - was at the club's training ground for the first time on Thursday for pre-season testing.

For managers, the challenge is not simply the absence itself. Players returning so late miss much of pre-season's tactical work, conditioning sessions and friendly matches, creating a difficult balancing act between preparation and recovery.

Manchester City and Arsenal, meanwhile, had the greatest concentration of players making deep runs into the competition.

City's World Cup contingent featured for several of the tournament's leading nations.

Rodri helped Spain win their second men's World Cup after playing 726 minutes, while Marc Guehi and Elliot Anderson helped England reach the final weekend.

Nico O'Reilly featured in England's semi-final run, while Erling Haaland and Jeremy Doku both reached the quarter-finals.

Arsenal's numbers were similarly striking.

Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka remained involved until England's 6-4 victory over France in the third-place play-off, while Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino reached the final with Spain.

William Saliba helped France reach the third-place play-off, although he was subsequently injured and did not feature again. Noni Madueke was part of England's run to the final weekend but did not play beyond the quarter-finals, while Martin Odegaard captained Norway to the quarter-finals.

The workload concerns are already being felt. City's Rodri recently had back surgery and is expected to miss a "short period" at the start of the season, while Saliba avoided surgery, but Arsenal have confirmed he will be sidelined for an "extended period" because of a back issue.

Even though neither setback can be attributed solely to the World Cup, both underline the physical demands being placed on players in an increasingly crowded football calendar.

Those clubs are likely to begin the campaign without having enjoyed a full pre-season with several key players.

The World Cup's biggest workload belonged to Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, who played all 810 minutes of Argentina's run to the final.

Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister ranked second among Premier League players with 749 minutes, while Spain midfielder Rodri was third on 726.

Several players effectively completed the equivalent of eight full matches during the tournament.

Goalkeepers naturally face different physical demands from outfield players, but the figures underline the extent of Premier League involvement throughout the competition.

With the players entitled to a minimum three-week break under Fifa regulations, for those involved in the final on 19 July - including Rodri, Porro, Zubimendi, Mac Allister, Enzo Fernandez, Emiliano Martinez and Lisandro Martinez - the earliest return date is 9 August.

Players who featured in England's third-place play-off will return a day earlier.

That leaves clubs with roughly 12 days to reintegrate some of their most important players before competitive football begins.

The concerns extend beyond this summer's World Cup.

Many of football's leading players have now experienced three consecutive summers of major tournaments, following Euro 2024 and Copa America, then last year's expanded Club World Cup and now the World Cup.

One of those players is Rodri, who warned in 2024 that footballers were "close" to striking because of workload concerns.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta and Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca have also voiced concerns about the demands being placed on elite players and the growing number of matches in the calendar.

The growing injury list during the World Cup provided another reminder of those concerns.

Aston Villa midfielder Amadou Onana suffered a serious knee injury while representing Belgium, while Manchester United and Uruguay defensive midfielder Manuel Ugarte saw his tournament cut short by injury. Reece James also had his minutes carefully managed by England as he continued his recovery from a hamstring problem.

For clubs such as Tottenham, Arsenal, Manchester City and Chelsea, the challenge is now immediate.

The World Cup has concluded. The countdown to the Premier League season is under way.

But for some players, recovery comes first, and the race to be ready for opening weekend has only just begun.

title: Trump beats world champion Wu to reach Shanghai final
description: World number one Judd Trump aims for his second Shanghai Masters title after beating world champion Wu Yize to reach this year's final.
fullText:
World number one Judd Trump will aim for his second Shanghai Masters title after beating world champion Wu Yize 10-6 to reach this year's final.

Wu, 22, took an early lead in his homeland and went on to make three century breaks at the first major event of the 2026-27 season.

But Trump recovered from a slow start to lead 4-2 and the 2019 world champion did enough to stay in front, compiling two century breaks of his own.

The 36-year-old Englishman will now play in his fifth Shanghai final, having claimed his first win in 2024.

He will face either Kyren Wilson or Zhao Xintong in Sunday's best-of-21 decider, with the second semi-final taking place on Saturday.

"It is always good to start quickly in Shanghai," said Trump. "Even though this isn't a ranking event, it fills you with confidence as you are against the best in the world.

"It will be a great game between Kyren and Xintong. It should be an exciting final whoever I face. It has been a good tournament so far, but you need to get over that line."

Wu edges past Murphy into Shanghai semi-finals

title: Connor stars as pacesetting Leeds thrash Toulouse
description: Leeds Rhinos retain their two-point cushion at the Super League summit as they thrash a depleted Toulouse side 46-0 at Headingley.
fullText:
Tries: Connor 2, Oledzki, Holroyd, McDonnell, Newman, Croft, Lumb Goals: Connor 7

Leeds Rhinos maintained their two-point cushion at the Super League summit as they thrashed a depleted Toulouse side 46-0 at Headingley.

Jake Connor lit up a stodgy first half, scoring the opener and teeing up Mikolaj Oledzki before his interception laid the foundations for Tom Holroyd's score shortly before half-time.

The table-toppers looked sharper after the break with James McDonnell, Harry Newman and Connor's second taking Rhinos 34 points clear.

Brodie Croft and Riley Lumb crossed in the final quarter, while Connor capped an impressive display with seven goals from eight attempts to finish with 22 points.

A 10th win from 10 on home turf this season keeps Leeds ahead of second-placed Wigan after their victory at Leigh.

Ruthless Wigan seize on Leigh errors to go second

Burgess scores 200th try as Hull KR beat Bradford

Toulouse had scored 106 points in their past two away trips, including a 46-0 whitewash of St Helens, but it was their turn to be scoreless on this occasion and they remain ninth after a 14th defeat of the campaign.

Ned McCormack was denied a sixth-minute score for Leeds in a stop-start opening when video referee Liam Rush spotted Chris Hankinson's knock-on.

But the Rhinos had the lead after 12 minutes when Connor dummied and cut back inside to score following Lumb's break.

Super League's leading points scorer this season was involved again as he teed up Oledzki to power over from close range.

Without injured playmaker Olly Ashall-Bott and fielding six academy graduates, Toulouse could not capitalise on good positions, with Tiaki Chan's surge halted five metres short after Luke Polselli's brilliant one-handed offload.

And Leeds pulled further clear when Presley Cassell's fine offload gave Holroyd a simple finish under the posts.

The hosts began the second half with more intent and within minutes, quick ball through the hands saw Croft send in McDonnell for his fifth try in three games.

Holroyd was held up over the line, while last-ditch defence denied Jarrod O'Connor and Lumb as Toulouse, to their credit, continued to fight.

But the incessant pressure told when Newman, playing just his third game on the wing in place of the injured Maika Sivo, went in at the right corner.

Connor, the 2025 Man of Steel, leapt high to grab Lachlan Miller's pinpoint kick under the posts and register his second score.

With the game long since won, Leeds rang the changes but still pressed for more.

Croft sniped through a gap for his 24th Super League try of the season, and Lumb finished in the left corner, before Connor's touchline conversion typified a clinical all-round display from the leaders.

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur told BBC Radio Leeds:

"It's the closest we've got to 80 minutes. I was pretty pleased with that performance. I thought we showed good resilience, good fight, the attitude was really good, too.

"I asked the boys for a bit extra tonight in their effort and physicality and they delivered.

"I thought the opposition were really good early, they made us fight and we were probably fortunate to go in [at half-time] at 18-0, but that's exactly what we needed.

"Our resilience before half-time and then even at the end of the game on the try line, just to keep turning up for each other, and that's an attitude thing, so I was really pleased with that."
